chunks: Hadith 5431 — ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥāzim al-Kalbī, the nephew of Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar — and he was not al-Jaʿfarī — from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever does not make his bequest well at the time of death, that is a deficiency in his dignity and intellect.”
It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, how does the dying person make a bequest?” He said: “When his death comes near and the people gather around him, he says:”

“O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. O Allah, I make a covenant with You in the abode of this world that I bear witness that there is no god but You, alone, without partner; and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; and that Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and that resurrection is true, and reckoning is true, and the sirat is true, and divine decree and the scale are true; and that the religion is as You have described, and that Islam is as You have legislated, and that the word is as You have conveyed, and that the Qur’an is as You have sent down, and that You are Allah, the Manifest Truth. May Allah reward Muḥammad on our behalf with the best reward, and may Allah greet Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad with peace. O Allah, O my provision at my distress, O my companion at my hardship, O guardian of my blessing, my God and the God of my forefathers, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, for if You leave me to myself, I would be nearer to evil and farther from good. So bring intimacy to my loneliness in the grave, and appoint for me a covenant spread open on the day I meet You.”

Then he makes bequest concerning his need. The confirmation of this bequest is in the Qur’an, in the surah in which Maryam is mentioned, in His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “They do not possess intercession except one who has taken a covenant with the All-beneficent.”

So this is the covenant of the dying person, and the bequest is a duty upon every Muslim, and it is incumbent upon him to preserve this bequest and teach it. And Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib صلوات الله عليه said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله taught it to me.” And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام taught it to me.”

key_terms.الصِّرَاطَ: the bridge or path associated with the afterlife passage
key_terms.الْحِسَابَ: the reckoning of deeds on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْمِيزَانَ: the scale by which deeds are weighed
key_terms.مُرُوءَتِهِ: his dignity, honorable conduct, and manly virtue
key_terms.وَصِيَّتَهُ: his bequest or final will made at death

ai.seo_question: What supplication and testimony should a Muslim recite when making a bequest at the time of death?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the form of a dying Muslim’s bequest, combining a testimony of faith, affirmation of key creedal truths, and a du'a for divine care at death and in the grave. It also links this covenantal will to Qur'an 19:87, presenting the وصيّة as something every Muslim should preserve and teach.
